senses.sense_definition: Either of two small square leather cases containing Hebrew texts, worn by Jewish men on the arm and forehead during weekday morning prayers.

examples.text: During morning prayers, the worshipper carefully bound the <w>phylactery</w> around his left arm.
Every Jewish male is traditionally expected to put on a <w>phylactery</w> upon reaching adulthood.

senses.sense_definition: An amulet or charm worn to provide magical protection or ward off evil.

examples.text: The knight carried a protective <w>phylactery</w> around his neck before entering the dark forest.
She believed the ancient <w>phylactery</w> would shield her household from misfortune.

traits.comment: used in historical or literary contexts

senses.sense_definition: In fantasy fiction, a magical vessel or enchanted object in which an undead creature, such as a lich, stores its soul.

examples.text: The adventurers could not defeat the undead sorcerer until they destroyed his hidden <w>phylactery</w>.
The wizard placed his soul into an ornate <w>phylactery</w> to achieve dark immortality.

senses.sense_definition: A painted or sculpted scroll containing speech or inscriptions, represented in medieval art as emerging from a figure's mouth or held in hand.

examples.text: In the medieval painting, the angel holds a flowing <w>phylactery</w> inscribed with a Latin phrase.
Art historians examine the words on each <w>phylactery</w> to identify the depicted characters.

senses.sense_definition: A receptacle or container used to display or protect holy religious relics.

examples.text: The saint's finger bone was preserved inside a small gilded <w>phylactery</w> in the chapel.
Centuries ago, the cathedral acquired a valuable <w>phylactery</w> crafted from gold and enamel.
